title: "17. Time-varying transmission: R_t under seasonal forcing and interventions"
subtitle: "ReproductiveNumbers.jl vignettes"
author: "Simon D. W. Frost"
date: today
---

## Overview

When the transmission rate varies in time, `β(t)`, there is no infection-free *steady*
state and `R₀` in the sense of an autonomous model is not defined (the package refuses to
compute it). The effective reproduction number is still well defined at every instant: it
is the next-generation construction with the current `β(t)` and the current susceptible
pool, `R_t = β(t) S(t) / (γ N)` for the SIR model. This vignette builds a seasonally forced
SIR model, adds a smooth intervention that reduces transmission for a period, and follows
`R_t` through the resulting epidemic waves.

Seasonally forced models have their own basic reproduction number, defined through the
spectral radius of a linear operator on periodic functions (Bacaër and Guernaoui 2006);
that is a different quantity, which the package does not compute.

## A seasonally forced SIR model

```{julia}
using ReproductiveNumbers, ModelingToolkit, Symbolics, OrdinaryDiffEqTsit5, Plots
using ModelingToolkit: t_nounits as t, D_nounits as D

@parameters β₀ ε γ N
@variables S(t) I(t) R(t)
β = β₀ * (1 + ε * cos(2π * t / 365))
sir = complete(System([D(S) ~ -β * S * I / N,
        D(I) ~ β * S * I / N - γ * I,
        D(R) ~ γ * I],
    t; name = :seasonal_sir))
```

Asking for `R₀` fails, with a message pointing to the effective reproduction number:

```{julia}
try
    next_generation_matrix(sir, [I]; equilibrium = Dict(S => N))
catch err
    err
end
```

`R_t` is a closed-form function of time and of the state:

```{julia}
Rt = effective_reproduction_number(sir, [I])
```

## R_t through the epidemic

```{julia}
sir_Rt, Rtvar = add_effective_reproduction_number(sir, [I])
p = [β₀ => 0.3, ε => 0.4, γ => 0.2, N => 1e6]
prob = ODEProblem(sir_Rt, [[S => 1e6 - 10, I => 10.0, R => 0.0]; p], (0.0, 3 * 365.0))
sol = solve(prob, Tsit5(); saveat = 1.0)
plt = plot(
    sol; idxs = [Rtvar], label = "R_t", xlabel = "day", ylabel = "R_t", legend = :topright)
hline!(plt, [1.0]; label = "threshold", linestyle = :dash)
```

Susceptible depletion and the seasonal cycle combine: the first wave ends when `R_t` falls
below one, but the return of the high-transmission season pushes `R_t` back above one and
produces a second wave.

```{julia}
plot(sol; idxs = [I], label = "I(t)", xlabel = "day")
```

The two contributions can be separated: the seasonal factor `β(t)/β₀`, and the
susceptible fraction `S(t)/N`.

```{julia}
plot(sol.t, [0.3 / 0.2 * (1 + 0.4 * cos(2π * τ / 365)) for τ in sol.t];
    label = "β(t)/γ (all susceptible)", xlabel = "day")
plot!(sol.t, sol[Rtvar]; label = "R_t")
hline!([1.0]; label = "threshold", linestyle = :dash)
```

## An intervention

Suppose transmission is reduced by a factor `1 - c` between days `t₁` and `t₂`, switched
on and off smoothly. The intervention is just another factor in `β(t)`, and `R_t` follows it.

```{julia}
@parameters c t₁ t₂ k
switch(τ) = 1 / (1 + exp(-k * (τ - t₁))) * (1 - 1 / (1 + exp(-k * (τ - t₂))))
β_int = β * (1 - c * switch(t))
sir_int = complete(System(
    [D(S) ~ -β_int * S * I / N,
        D(I) ~ β_int * S * I / N - γ * I,
        D(R) ~ γ * I],
    t; name = :seasonal_sir_intervention))
sir_int_Rt, Rtvar_int = add_effective_reproduction_number(sir_int, [I])
p_int = [p; c => 0.5; t₁ => 60.0; t₂ => 150.0; k => 0.5]
prob_int = ODEProblem(
    sir_int_Rt, [[S => 1e6 - 10, I => 10.0, R => 0.0]; p_int], (0.0, 3 * 365.0))
sol_int = solve(prob_int, Tsit5(); saveat = 1.0)
plt = plot(sol.t, sol[Rtvar]; label = "no intervention", xlabel = "day", ylabel = "R_t")
plot!(plt, sol_int.t, sol_int[Rtvar_int]; label = "intervention, days 60-150")
hline!(plt, [1.0]; label = "threshold", linestyle = :dash)
```

```{julia}
plot(sol.t, sol[I]; label = "no intervention", xlabel = "day", ylabel = "I(t)")
plot!(sol_int.t, sol_int[I]; label = "intervention")
```

The intervention brings `R_t` below one during the first season, but leaves more
susceptibles for the following one, which then produces a larger second wave: a familiar
lesson that `R_t` makes visible directly.

## Evaluating without rebuilding the system

The same trajectory can be obtained from any solution of the original system, with the
numeric next-generation matrix evaluated at each saved time (this also works when no closed
form exists):

```{julia}
ngm = next_generation_matrix(sir, [I]; equilibrium = Dict(), autonomous = false)
prob0 = ODEProblem(sir, [[S => 1e6 - 10, I => 10.0, R => 0.0]; p], (0.0, 3 * 365.0))
sol0 = solve(prob0, Tsit5(); saveat = 30.0)
effective_reproduction_number(ngm, sol0)
```
